name: Tesla

Software Engineer.dsaDepth: Heavy — a genuinely unusual order (hiring-manager call BEFORE any technical evaluation), first-principles depth-probing on fundamentals, and for final rounds a written "Evidence of Excellence" submission
rounds: Hiring-manager call (30-45 min) — distinctively comes BEFORE any technical round, assessing team fit and technical depth at a conversational level
Online assessment (85-90 min, Codility/HackerRank, ~3 problems, easy-medium, under time pressure)
Technical screen (~60 min live coding): practical problem solving, explicitly including catching your own bugs, not just reaching a working answer

Panel rounds (3-5 rounds, 45-60 min each): coding (LeetCode-medium, strings/arrays common), system design, first-principles depth (language internals, memory, architecture, and for some teams physics-adjacent reasoning), and behavioral, sometimes closing with a senior-leadership round
Evidence of Excellence (final rounds, increasingly common): a 1-2 page WRITTEN submission describing your single most significant technical achievement, evaluated for impact, ownership and complexity
extraTopics: First-principles depth-probing — interviewers push into how things actually work (memory, architecture, sometimes physics-adjacent reasoning for hardware-adjacent teams), not just correctness
Writing, not just talking, about your best work for the Evidence of Excellence submission
Team variance is large — Autopilot, vehicle firmware, energy, manufacturing systems and internal-tools teams run meaningfully different loops
Software Engineer.notes: Overall difficulty is rated 3.9/5 on Glassdoor — comparable to Google/Meta but with a different texture (less exotic algorithms, more depth-probing and pressure tolerance). Total process length is reported around 34 days on average, though individual reports range from 2 weeks to 3 months.
